title: Choose the visual world — re-roll 1
question: New hand after your re-roll. Keep the rolled direction, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Der Lichtkasten
options.lineage: 1971 pocket airline timetable on a light table
options.thesis: The whole app is a lit timetable bed under tinted slides: one type size everywhere, rank carried by weight, case, reversal and rule — and the selected store is the one light travelling the bed.
options.viewport: Map home as the lit bed: goldenrod shell, ivory slides (navbar, sidebar, cards) raked 0 in layout but lit from one corner, one type size at four weights; the selected store's slide goes opaque reversed and the pin halo pulses with the travelling-light easing.
options.risk: One-size type can flatten hierarchy into monotony if weight steps stay timid.

raised.raise: Travelling-light motion adopts the overshoot settle (0.4s, overshoot-then-settle curve) from the zoo guide-map world.
The store photo viewer keeps the feed's full-bleed snap: one photo per viewport, snap paging, no partial state.

options.label: Der Gartenplan
options.thesis: Every area is a swelling flat-colour lobe on cream water; the coastline does the dividing and a live capsule rides the coast.
options.viewport: Cream ground, green guide lobes for store kinds, capsule chips in yellow/coral/blue, one grotesk at 0.95 leading; the map reads as a friendly guide map.
options.case: Holds audience (day-tripper warmth, family-friendliness); loses product clarity: the lobe topology fights a real OSM basemap instead of decorating it.
options.risk: Flat colour lobes can read as a children's map when density rises.

options.label: Der Fahrplan-Atlas
options.thesis: Results as timetable rows in a ruled atlas grid — distances as minutes, kinds as small code strips.
options.viewport: Ivory ground, ruled row grid, condensed caps for destinations, amber accent for the active leg.
options.case: Holds clarity (timetable rows fit stores well); loses audience: it is the transit rider's world, not the shopper's.
options.risk: Reads as a transit app for shopping data.

options.label: Datamatics
options.viewport: Pure B/W barber-pole field with monospace numerics.
options.case: Fuses poorly: strobing data-sublime is spectacle a shopping finder cannot carry; kills kind-color semantics.
options.kept: Tabular-numerics discipline (all figures in monospace tabular cells).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The modern map-app UI played straight at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Floating search, white cards, gray map chrome — the arrangement visitors expect.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Google Maps by design.
